design.affected_system: coastal protection, evacuation, and long-term adaptation system
alternatives: harden critical nodes and add backup power
use adaptive recovery portfolios robust to correlated failures
assumptions: Elevation, surge, shoreline, asset, and population layers share documented vertical and horizontal datums.
Sea-level pathways, damage functions, and adaptation performance remain explicit scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: Existing defenses and continuity plans face compound failure without added measures.

constraints.description: Life-safety and critical-service thresholds must hold under severe correlated failure scenarios.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: coastal resilience director and emergency-management commissioner
design.decision_question: Which adaptation and continuity strategy survives surge, rain, wind, power, access, and supply-chain failures?

independence_key.binding_constraint: Life-safety and critical-service thresholds must hold under severe correlated failure scenarios.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Hazard dependence, fragility, restoration, demand, and adaptation-performance ranges have documented validation.

design.intended_claim: A versioned stress-test design for comparing declared alternatives affecting compound coastal continuity strategy, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in scenario-weighted critical service outage duration
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not describe synthetic compound failures as forecast probabilities without calibrated dependence evidence.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Hazard dependence, fragility, restoration, demand, and adaptation-performance ranges have documented validation.

design.title: Stress-test coastal systems under compound failure
transportability_risks: Coastal morphology, tides, subsidence, protection standards, and evacuation behavior differ.
Long-horizon adaptation values depend on local finance, land tenure, and legal authority.

family.affected_system: coastal protection, evacuation, and long-term adaptation system
claim_boundary: Hazard observations and modeled exposure do not establish individual harm or causation.
Proposed adaptations are planning alternatives, not adopted policy or engineered designs.
A design-only record is not a city execution, validated forecast, or impact result.
family.decision_owner: coastal resilience director and emergency-management commissioner
family.description: Decision designs for coastal exposure diagnosis, surge forecasting, adaptation portfolios, protective siting, emergency allocation, closure timing, compound stress, and evaluation.
family.title: Coastal storms and sea-level adaptation

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
